messages:
alex: noticed p99 decode latency jump on host preparse after the kernel-selector rollout ~03:00 UTC. p99 +40-55ms. flamegraph: https://perf.example.com/fg/4321987650 :thinking_face:

infra-bot: perf-alert: host-preparse.p99 latency +48ms vs baseline; affected pods: host-runtime-3a*, host-runtime-3b*

maria: can you paste the flamegraph top stacks or a short sample? is this in the parser or tokenization step?

alex: top stacks point to Tokenizer::slice -> proto::unpack -> grpc::writev (many tiny writev calls). quick grep from perf trace:

```
# sample stacks (collapsed)
Tokenize::slice  34.7ms
proto::unpack     22.1ms
grpc::writev      18.9ms
Scheduler::poll    5.2ms
```

cheng: hmm. kernel-selector swapped to `avx-fused` for short-seq path in the rollout. that kernel does an extra alignment copy to satisfy vector loads. locally i repro'd with short sequences and saw ~+35ms p99. command i ran:

```
$ ./bench --seq=32 --batch=16 --kernel=avx-fused --trace=stack
# result: p50 9ms, p95 28ms, p99 47ms (baseline p99 ~12ms)
```

sam: @alex @cheng could KV cache churn be amplifying this? more misses -> more full-tokenize work on host. any change in kv hit rates?

alex: dug into kv metrics: baseline hit ~92% for short requests, after rollout hit ~88% for those clients. so small but correlates with spike windows. logs show more prefix-miss from client-service-A between 03:05-03:20 UTC.

maria: batching heuristics might be falling back because kernel cost estimator changed after selector swap. smaller batches => more grpc smallwrites => writev overhead dominates. did the rollout update kernel cost table?

cheng: it didn't — we swapped selector but didn't refresh the static cost table for `avx-fused`. selector now picks kernel based on sequence length only and assumes old cost. net result: batching policy reduced batch targets. short-term mitigation: clamp the kernel_cost estimate for `avx-fused` to the baseline value until rebench.

alex: i'm pushing a tiny patch to force fallback kernel for seq < 64 on hosts in canary while we rebench. patch (very small):

```
- if (seq_len < 64) choose_kernel = selector.pick(seq_len);
+ if (seq_len < 64) choose_kernel = selector.pick(seq_len) == avx_fused ? fallback_kernel : selector.pick(seq_len);
```

maria: can we flip this as a feature-flag so we don't need full restart? ops can toggle.

alex: ops, can you roll the flag to canary? flag: `kernel.force_fallback_shortseq=true`

deploy-bot: flag update applied to canary at 04:15 UTC (kernel.force_fallback_shortseq=true)

alex: monitoring canary now — early signs p99 trending down.

sam: i'll add a KV prefetch probe and a short synthetic with mixed short/long sequences to measure miss amplification. will post results in this thread.

maria: next steps (short):
- rebench avx-fused vs fallback for seq in [8,32,64] (cheng)
- update kernel cost table used by batching heuristics (maria)
- add kernel-selection telemetry (per-request kernel id) for 24h (alex)
- run KV-prefetch probe and correlate misses with batching size (sam)

alex: assigning owners: @cheng rebench, @maria update batching cost table + telemetry hook, @sam kv probe. i'll keep watching infra graphs and will rollback flag if we see regressions. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: note: creating perf-regression alert rule: host-preparse.p99 delta > 20ms for 10m -> paging oncall.

alex: thanks all — will follow up with a short postmortem once we have rebench numbers.
